q1_issues.issue: The bare plural "undesired suitors" is encoded as a single singular witness `sk_suitor_1`, so number is lost and `undesired` is predicated of one individual rather than distributed over a group or kind.

"PeopleSoft management" is a bare noun-noun sequence, and the possessive rule's own part/component test makes management a component of the company (-> `PartOf`); `Possession` is licensed for 's, possessive pronouns and genitive of-phrases.
"known as a 'poison pill'" is flattened into a plain type atom on the defense, dropping the appellation layer that the participial post-modifier (reduced relative) rule says to give event form.

q2_gaps: Appellation post-modifier "known as / called <NP>": the reduced-relative rule demands an event, but no encoding is licensed for the predicative "as" complement, and an indefinite "a 'poison pill'" is a class label rather than a `Name` string.
"could" is absent from the modal sense-map (must -> Must/Obligated, may -> Might/Permitted, can -> Can/Permitted), so nothing fixes whether "could choose" is capability, epistemic or deontic.

A proper-noun modifier naming a distinct possessor ("PeopleSoft management"): the naming section covers name-plus-kind ("the Brindle estuary" -> `(Member brindle estuary)`) but not a name denoting a separate entity the head noun belongs to.
notes: The control-verb handling of "choose to activate" (complement event at top level, `Theme` link, no status of its own, subject control copied in) and the reduced relative "designed to thwart …" with its `To` purpose atom follow the instruction set exactly, as does keeping `poison_pill` undecomposed.
